steps.say: Every sound is made by something vibrating. Touch your throat while you hum to feel the vibrations.
Vibrations travel through solids, liquids and gases to your ears. Sound cannot travel through empty space.

figure.alt: A drum making a sound that travels to an ear.

steps.say: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. Faster vibrations make higher notes.
Short, thin or tight things vibrate faster. A short angklung tube makes a higher note than a long one.
Loudness depends on the size of the vibrations. Hitting a drum harder makes bigger vibrations and a louder sound.
Soft materials like curtains and foam absorb sound. They are used to make rooms quieter.

check.prompt: How can you make a guitar string play a higher note?

options.why: A looser string vibrates more slowly and plays a lower note.
Plucking gently makes the note quieter, not higher.
Thicker strings vibrate more slowly and play lower notes.

hints: Higher notes come from faster vibrations.
Tight, thin and short strings vibrate faster.
Cross out the choices that slow the vibrations down or only change loudness.
check.explanation: Tightening a string makes it vibrate faster, so it plays a higher note.

check.prompt: Bigger vibrations make a sound more ___.
hints: Big vibrations and small vibrations sound different.
Hitting a drum harder makes bigger vibrations.
Think of the word that is the opposite of quiet.
check.explanation: Bigger vibrations make louder sounds, and smaller vibrations make quieter sounds.
